name.text: Circumradius and a chord: find the inscribed angle (INNODEMS)

questiontext.text:
In the circle below with centre \(O\), the chord \(BC = {@BC@}\) cm and the circumradius is \(R = {@RR@}\) cm.

Using \(A\), \(B\), \(C\) on the circle as shown, find the angle \(\theta = \angle BAC\), in degrees.

generalfeedback.text:
Drop a perpendicular from the centre \(O\) to the midpoint \(M\) of the chord \(BC\). This makes a right-angled triangle \(OMB\) in which \(OB = R\), \(BM = \tfrac12 BC\), and \(\angle BOM = \theta\) (half the central angle \(\angle BOC = 2\theta\), which is itself twice the inscribed angle \(\theta\)).

[[/jsxgraph]]

From triangle \(OMB\):

\[ \sin\theta = \frac{BM}{OB} = \frac{\tfrac12 BC}{R} = \frac{BC}{2R} = \frac{ {@BC@} }{2\cdot {@RR@}} = {@sinexact@}. \]

Taking the inverse sine (and reading the acute angle shown at \(A\)):

\[ \theta = {@theta@}^\circ. \]

truefeedback.text: Remember that \(\sin\theta = \sin(180^\circ-\theta)\), so the sine value alone gives two possible angles. The triangle drawn has an acute angle at \(A\) — choose that one.

node.description: Gave sin(theta) instead of the angle?

truefeedback.text: That looks like the value of \(\sin\theta = \dfrac{BC}{2R}\), not the angle itself. Take the inverse sine of it to find \(\theta\).
That looks like the central angle \(\angle BOC\) rather than \(\theta = \angle BAC\). What's the relationship between angles at the centre and angles at the circumference?
